search_log: Searched “Geraldine Brooks Horse novel point of view first person third person alternating narrators” and opened the explicit eNotes structural analysis.

Searched “Horse Geraldine Brooks excerpt Thomas J Scott I narrator,” “read an excerpt,” and publisher/author-site variants; located and opened the authorized Hachette/Viking opening extract and the permissioned BookBrowse excerpt.

Searched exact first-person quote fragments and Thomas Scott diary terms; results corroborated recurring Scott material but did not yield an authorized whole-book source explicitly labeling the book ALTERNATING.

Checked the official author page, Viking Q&A, Google Books record, Kirkus review, BookRags chapter analysis, and study-guide results. The official materials verified timelines and edition but did not explicitly state first/third-person alternation; some generic study guides incorrectly reduced the novel to third person.
No two Tier A/B sources were found whose supports field could responsibly be ALTERNATING; the two Tier A excerpts establish only the THIRD opening component, so confidence is medium.
person_note: The novel alternates sustained grammatical persons: most Theo, Jess, Jarret, Martha Jackson, and related chapters are third-person, while recurring Thomas Scott diary or documentary chapters are first-person. The quote set strongly samples the third-person chapters and includes two attributable Scott I passages (q07329 and q07333). Other first-person material is treated as embedded or unresolved where speech/document boundaries are clipped, especially q07322 and q07339. The whole-book alternation is explicit in one credible structural source, but the Tier A sources cover only the third-person opening and therefore do not independently support ALTERNATING as a complete structure. Because there are not two Tier A/B entries whose supports value is exactly ALTERNATING, confidence is med rather than high.
